stem: An NSG contains a custom inbound rule 'Deny-All-TCP' (priority 300, TCP, any source, any port, Deny) and 'Allow-HTTPS' (priority 400, TCP 443 from Internet, Allow). A client on the internet connects to TCP 443. What happens?

options.text: Allowed, because Allow-HTTPS is more specific.
options.explanation: Specificity is irrelevant. Rules are processed by priority number only.
Correct. Priority 300 is evaluated before 400 and matches, so processing stops with Deny.
The default rule is never reached because a custom rule matched first.

options.text: Allowed, because allow rules are evaluated before deny rules.
options.explanation: There is no allow-before-deny ordering; only priority matters.

explanation: NSG rules are evaluated from the lowest to the highest priority number, and the first match decides. Fix it by giving Allow-HTTPS a priority lower than 300.

stem: Web VMs (NICs in ASG 'asg-web') and SQL VMs (NICs in ASG 'asg-sql') are in different subnets of the same VNet. SQL must accept TCP 1433 only from web VMs. The SQL subnet NSG has only default rules. Which configuration meets the requirement with the fewest rules?

options.text: Allow TCP 1433 from asg-web to asg-sql (priority 100).
options.explanation: Not enough: AllowVnetInBound (65000) still allows 1433 from every other VNet source.

options.text: Allow TCP 1433 from asg-web to asg-sql (priority 100) and deny TCP 1433 from VirtualNetwork to asg-sql (priority 200).
options.explanation: Correct. The ASG allow matches web VMs first; every other VNet source hits the deny before reaching AllowVnetInBound.
Internet traffic is already denied by DenyAllInBound; this does nothing for VNet sources.

options.text: Delete AllowVnetInBound and add an allow from asg-web.

explanation: Because AllowVnetInBound permits all VirtualNetwork sources, restricting east-west traffic needs an explicit deny placed after the specific allow.

stem: Which TWO statements about application security groups are true?

options.text: All network interfaces in an ASG must belong to the same virtual network.
options.explanation: Correct, this is a documented ASG constraint.

options.text: An ASG can be used as the source or destination of an NSG rule.
options.explanation: Correct. That is the purpose of ASGs.

options.text: An ASG can be associated with a subnet instead of an NSG.
options.explanation: ASGs are applied to NIC IP configurations, not subnets, and they contain no rules.

options.text: ASGs contain their own allow and deny rules.
options.explanation: ASGs are just groupings; rules live in NSGs.

explanation: ASGs group NICs so NSG rules can refer to workloads instead of IP addresses.

stem: VM1 has a Standard public IP. The subnet NSG allows TCP 443 from Internet at priority 200. The NIC has its own NSG with only default rules. HTTPS connections from the internet time out. What is the cause?

options.text: The NIC NSG's DenyAllInBound blocks the traffic after the subnet NSG allows it.
options.explanation: Correct. Inbound traffic must be allowed by both the subnet NSG and the NIC NSG.

options.text: The subnet NSG needs an outbound rule for return traffic.
options.explanation: NSGs are stateful, so no outbound rule is needed for responses.

options.text: Standard public IPs cannot accept inbound traffic.
options.explanation: They can, once an NSG allows it. They are closed by default only.

options.text: The NIC NSG is evaluated first and the subnet NSG is ignored.
options.explanation: For inbound traffic the subnet NSG is evaluated first, then the NIC NSG; neither is ignored.

explanation: Use Effective security rules on the NIC or IP flow verify: both show the NIC-level DenyAllInBound as the deciding rule.

stem: You run the command below. What does it return?
code:
az network watcher test-ip-flow -g rg-web --vm vm-web-01 --direction Inbound \
  --protocol TCP --local 10.0.1.4:22 --remote 203.0.113.10:50123

options.text: Whether the flow is allowed or denied, and the name of the NSG rule that decided it.
options.explanation: Correct. IP flow verify evaluates the effective NSG rules for one 5-tuple.

options.text: A packet capture of SSH traffic to the VM.
options.explanation: That is Network Watcher packet capture, a different feature.

options.text: The next hop for traffic from 10.0.1.4.
options.explanation: That is Next hop, which tests routing, not NSGs.

options.text: The latency between the VM and 203.0.113.10.
options.explanation: That is Connection Monitor / connection troubleshoot.

explanation: IP flow verify answers 'would this flow be allowed?' with the deciding rule. It does not send real traffic.

stem: Put the evaluation steps for an inbound TCP flow from the internet to a VM (Standard public IP, NSGs on both subnet and NIC) in the correct order.

options.text: Subnet NSG rules evaluated by priority; first match decides
Packet arrives at the public IP
NIC NSG rules evaluated by priority; first match decides
Packet delivered to the VM; return traffic allowed automatically

explanation: Inbound: subnet NSG first, then NIC NSG. Outbound reverses the order. Statefulness means the response needs no extra rule.

stem: A team must create and manage all resources in a resource group but must NOT be able to grant access to others. Which built-in role follows least privilege?

options.explanation: Owner can also assign roles, which violates the requirement.
Correct. Contributor manages everything but its NotActions exclude Microsoft.Authorization writes.
Manages access only; cannot create resources.

explanation: Contributor = Actions '*' minus Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write, /*/Delete and elevateAccess.

stem: Operators must start, stop and resize VMs in a subscription but must not modify virtual networks or storage accounts. What should you assign?

options.text: Virtual Machine Contributor at the subscription
options.explanation: Correct. It covers VM management without granting VNet or storage account management.
That role is for signing in to the VM OS with Entra ID, not managing the VM resource.
Grants networking, the opposite of the requirement.

explanation: Job-function built-in roles are the least-privilege choice when they fit.

stem: You assign Reader to User1 at management group MG1. Subscription Sub1 is under MG1 and contains RG1. User1 also has Contributor on RG1. What can User1 do in RG2 (also in Sub1)?

options.explanation: Correct. Reader is inherited from MG1; the Contributor assignment applies only to RG1 and its children.
Contributor at RG1 does not flow sideways to RG2.

options.text: Nothing; management group assignments do not apply to resource groups
options.explanation: Management group assignments inherit to all subscriptions, resource groups and resources below.

explanation: Assignments inherit downward only. Effective access in a scope is the union of assignments at that scope and its ancestors.

stem: Which command grants the group 'Ops' the Reader role on resource group rg-web only?

options.text: az role assignment create --assignee-object-id <ops-id> --assignee-principal-type Group --role Reader --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/rg-web
options.explanation: Correct: explicit group object ID and resource group scope.
Subscription scope is wider than required.

options.text: az ad group member add --group Ops --role Reader
options.explanation: az ad group member add manages group membership; it has no --role argument.

options.text: az role definition create --role Reader --scope rg-web
options.explanation: role definition create defines a custom role; it does not assign one.

explanation: Role assignment = principal + role definition + scope.

stem: User2 has Contributor on RG1 and is a member of group G1, which has User Access Administrator on Sub1 (the parent of RG1). Can User2 create a role assignment on RG1?

options.text: No, Contributor's NotActions deny Microsoft.Authorization writes.
options.explanation: NotActions are not denies. They only subtract from the Contributor role.

options.text: Yes, User Access Administrator is inherited from Sub1 through G1.
options.explanation: Correct. RBAC is additive across all assignments and groups.

options.text: No, group-based assignments do not apply to role management.
options.explanation: Group assignments apply exactly like direct ones.

options.text: Only after a deny assignment is created.
options.explanation: A deny assignment would block access, not grant it.

explanation: Effective permissions are the union of every applicable assignment; only deny assignments subtract.

stem: Match each requirement to the tool that answers it.

options.text: Microsoft Entra ID > Roles and administrators

pairs.left: List a user's effective Azure role assignments at a resource group, including inherited and group-based ones
Find why Owner cannot delete a resource deployed by a managed application
See who can reset passwords for users in the tenant

explanation: Azure RBAC tools live under Access control (IAM) on a scope; directory permissions are Entra roles.

stem: Which redundancy option keeps data readable and writable if one availability zone in the primary region fails, at the lowest cost?

options.explanation: All three LRS copies are in one datacenter.
Correct. Three synchronous copies across three zones.
Primary copies are LRS; a zone failure can make the data unavailable until recovery or failover.
It works, but it costs more than ZRS for a requirement that only covers zones.

explanation: ZRS is the cheapest option that tolerates a zone failure for both reads and writes.

stem: An app must keep reading blobs during a full regional outage without anyone initiating a failover. Blobs are moved to the archive tier after 180 days. Which redundancy option do you choose?

options.explanation: Readable secondary, but the archive tier is not supported on zone-redundant accounts.
Correct. It has a readable secondary endpoint and supports the archive tier.
No readable secondary without failover, and no archive tier.

explanation: Combine two constraints: RA- for secondary reads, and archive tier support (LRS, GRS and RA-GRS only).

stem: A GRS account's primary region is down. You plan a customer-managed failover. Which TWO statements are correct?

options.text: Writes made after the Last Sync Time may be lost.
After the failover the account is LRS in the new primary region.
options.explanation: Correct for an unplanned failover; reconfigure geo-redundancy afterwards.

options.text: Failover guarantees zero data loss because Azure keeps six copies.
options.explanation: Copy count does not change the asynchronous gap.

options.text: Reads from the secondary were available throughout the outage.
options.explanation: Only RA-GRS/RA-GZRS provide secondary reads before failover.

explanation: Check geoReplicationStats.lastSyncTime before failing over to understand potential loss.

stem: How many IP addresses can you assign to resources in an Azure subnet 10.1.0.0/26?

options.explanation: That is the total size of a /26.
On-premises convention (minus network and broadcast); Azure reserves more.
Azure reserves exactly five, not six.

explanation: Azure reserves the network address, .1, .2, .3 and the broadcast address in every subnet.

stem: VNet1 uses 10.0.0.0/16. You must create VNet2 and later peer it with VNet1. Which address space can you use for VNet2?

options.explanation: Contains VNet1's range, so it overlaps.

explanation: Peered VNets must have non-overlapping address spaces.

stem: You are planning subnets in a hub VNet. Which TWO subnet configurations are valid as written?

options.explanation: Correct. Exact name and a recommended size.
Correct. Bastion requires this name and /26 or larger.
Azure subnets must be /29 or larger.

explanation: Gateway and Bastion subnets require exact names; Bastion requires /26 or larger.

stem: You assign the built-in 'Allowed locations' policy (West Europe only) to a subscription. The subscription already contains a storage account in East US. What happens to that storage account?

options.text: It is deleted at the next evaluation cycle.
It is moved to West Europe.
options.explanation: Policy cannot move resources between regions.

options.text: It keeps running and is reported as non-compliant.
options.explanation: Correct. Existing resources are evaluated and flagged; Deny applies only to new create/update requests.

options.text: All operations on it are blocked until it complies.
options.explanation: Deny only evaluates create/update requests, and does not block reads or deletes.

explanation: A new assignment changes nothing that already exists. It reports compliance, and Deny blocks future non-compliant create/update requests.

stem: Every resource must carry a costCenter tag. Resources should copy it from their resource group automatically, and existing resources must be fixed too. Which configuration meets the requirement?

options.text: Assign 'Inherit a tag from the resource group if missing' (Modify) with a managed identity, then create a remediation task.
options.explanation: Correct. Modify fixes new requests; the remediation task uses the managed identity to fix existing resources.

options.text: Add the costCenter tag to each resource group; resources inherit it.
options.explanation: Tags are not inherited by default.
It blocks new untagged resources but does not copy values or fix existing resources.

options.text: Apply a ReadOnly lock until resources are tagged.
options.explanation: Locks block changes; they do not add tags.

explanation: Modify and DeployIfNotExists can remediate existing resources only through a remediation task, which runs as the assignment's managed identity.

stem: You plan to enforce a new Deny policy in production but want to see which deployments it would block first, without breaking any. What should you do?

options.text: Assign it with enforcementMode set to DoNotEnforce, then review compliance.
options.explanation: Correct. Effects are not enforced, but compliance is still evaluated and reported.

options.text: Assign it with the Disabled effect.
options.explanation: Disabled skips evaluation entirely, so you learn nothing.

options.text: Assign it to an empty resource group.
options.explanation: Nothing is in scope, so it tells you nothing about production.
Exempt resources are not reported as non-compliant.

explanation: DoNotEnforce (portal: Policy enforcement Disabled) is designed for what-if testing of policy impact.

stem: Order the Azure Policy effects as they are evaluated for a create request.

options.text: AuditIfNotExists / DeployIfNotExists (after the resource provider responds)

explanation: Because Modify runs before Deny, a Modify policy can make a request compliant before a Deny policy checks it.

stem: What does this command do?

options.text: Restricts new resources in the subscription to West Europe, except in rg-sandbox.
options.explanation: Correct. notScopes excludes rg-sandbox and everything in it.

options.text: Restricts only rg-sandbox to West Europe.
options.explanation: notScopes is an exclusion, not the target.
That is az policy definition create.

options.text: Moves existing resources to West Europe.

explanation: An assignment = definition + scope + parameters (+ notScopes, enforcement mode).

stem: You add the tag environment=prod to resource group RG1. RG1 contains VM1. Which tags does VM1 have?

options.explanation: Tags are not inherited from resource groups.

options.text: Only the tags applied directly to VM1
environment=prod after the next compliance scan
options.explanation: Only a Modify policy plus remediation would add it.

options.text: All tags of RG1 and of the subscription
options.explanation: No tag inheritance exists by default.

explanation: Use Azure Policy (Modify) to copy tags from the resource group or subscription.

stem: A finance analyst must add and change tags on all resources in a subscription but must not modify the resources themselves. Which role should you assign?

options.explanation: Grants full resource management, so it is over-privileged.
Correct. It manages tags without granting access to the resources.

explanation: Tag Contributor is the least-privilege built-in role for tag management.

stem: A VM already has the tags owner=ana and environment=dev. You run the command below. Which tags does the VM have afterwards?
code: az tag update --resource-id <vm-id> --operation Merge --tags environment=prod costCenter=CC-100

options.explanation: That would be the result of --operation Replace.
Correct. Merge adds new tags and updates existing keys, keeping the others.
Merge overwrites the value of an existing key.
That resembles --operation Delete for the listed tags.

explanation: az tag update supports Merge, Replace and Delete operations.

stem: RG1 has a CanNotDelete lock. A user with the Owner role tries to resize VM1 in RG1 and then delete it. What happens?

options.text: Both operations succeed because the user is an Owner.
options.explanation: Locks apply to everyone, including Owners.

options.text: The resize succeeds; the delete fails.

options.explanation: That would be a ReadOnly lock.

options.text: The resize fails; the delete succeeds.
options.explanation: The reverse of the actual behaviour.

explanation: The Owner could remove the lock first (Owner has Microsoft.Authorization/locks/*), but while the lock exists the delete is blocked.

stem: After a ReadOnly lock is applied to a storage account, users who browse containers in the portal using access keys get an authorization error. Data in the account is unchanged. Why?

options.text: ReadOnly locks encrypt the data with a new key.
Listing account keys is a POST operation, which ReadOnly blocks.
options.explanation: Correct. Without keys, key-based data access in the portal fails; Entra ID data roles still work.

options.text: ReadOnly locks block all data-plane reads.
options.explanation: Locks do not apply to the data plane.

options.text: The lock rotated the access keys.

explanation: ReadOnly blocks every control-plane write, including POST actions such as listKeys.

stem: Storage account ST1 in RG1 has a CanNotDelete lock. RG1 itself has no lock. Which TWO statements are true?

options.explanation: Correct. A resource group cannot be deleted while it contains a locked resource.

options.text: A user with data-plane permissions can still delete blobs in ST1.
options.explanation: Correct. Locks protect the control plane only.

options.text: Other resources in RG1 also cannot be deleted.
options.explanation: The lock is on ST1 only; it is not inherited by siblings.

options.text: A Contributor can remove the lock.

explanation: Locks inherit downward, block deletion of their containers, and do not cover data operations.

stem: You move a VM, its managed disk and NIC from RG1 (West Europe) to RG2 (whose location is North Europe). Where does the VM run after the move?

options.text: North Europe, because RG2 is there.
options.explanation: A resource group's location only stores its metadata; moves never change a resource's region.

options.text: West Europe; only its resource ID changes.
options.explanation: Correct. Region changes need Azure Resource Mover or a redeployment.

options.text: Both regions during a migration window.
The move fails because the regions differ.
options.explanation: Resources in a group can be in any region.

explanation: Moving changes the resource group in the resource ID, not the region.

stem: Move validation for VM1 to another resource group fails. VM1 uses managed disk Disk1 and network interface NIC1 in the same source group. What should you do?

options.text: Move VM1, Disk1 and NIC1 in the same operation.
options.explanation: Correct. Dependent resources must be moved together.
Running state is not the cause of a dependency validation failure.
That breaks the VM; move it with the VM instead.

options.text: Apply a CanNotDelete lock to the source group.
options.explanation: Locks do not help a move.

explanation: Validation checks that every dependency is part of the move.

stem: What does this command do?

options.text: Deletes rg-old and every resource in it, returning without waiting for completion.
options.explanation: Correct. --no-wait returns immediately; deletion continues in the background.

options.text: Deletes rg-old only if it is empty.
options.explanation: Resource group deletion removes all contained resources.

options.text: Moves rg-old's resources to the default group, then deletes it.

explanation: Locks on any resource inside the group make the deletion fail.

stem: You must move subscription Sub1 from tenant Contoso to tenant Fabrikam's directory. What happens to existing Azure role assignments in Sub1?

options.text: They are kept and mapped to matching users in Fabrikam.
They are permanently deleted and must be re-created.
options.explanation: Correct. Plan role, managed-identity and Key Vault updates beforehand.

options.text: They are suspended until Fabrikam approves.

options.explanation: All Azure role assignments are removed.

explanation: Changing directory is different from transferring billing ownership.

stem: Deploying an Azure Container Instance fails with MissingSubscriptionRegistration. What is the fix?

options.explanation: Correct. The resource provider must be registered in the subscription.

options.text: Move the subscription to another management group.
options.explanation: Management groups do not register providers.

options.text: Assign the Contributor role to Microsoft.ContainerInstance.
options.explanation: Providers are registered, not assigned roles.

explanation: Registration is per subscription; the portal often registers providers automatically, but CLI/IaC deployments may need it explicitly.

stem: Which statement about Azure subscriptions is true?

options.text: A subscription trusts exactly one Microsoft Entra tenant.
options.explanation: Correct. A tenant can have many subscriptions.

options.text: A subscription can belong to several management groups.
Quotas are shared across all subscriptions in a tenant.
options.explanation: Quotas are per subscription (often per region).
A resource group lives in one subscription.

explanation: Subscriptions are billing, quota and access boundaries tied to one directory.

stem: A 1,000 USD monthly budget on a subscription reaches 100% of actual cost mid-month. What happens to running VMs?

options.explanation: Budgets never stop resources by themselves.

options.text: Nothing, unless an action group runs automation to stop them.
They are deallocated but not deleted.
options.explanation: Only your own automation would do that.

explanation: Use action groups (runbook, Logic App, Function) when you want an automated reaction.

stem: You want an email when the forecast shows the month will exceed the budget, and an automation runbook to run at 90% of actual spend. Which TWO settings do you configure on a resource-group budget?

options.text: An alert condition of type Forecasted at 100% with email recipients
An alert condition of type Actual at 90% linked to an action group that runs the runbook
options.explanation: Correct. Action groups are supported for resource group and subscription budgets.
Locks are not triggered by costs.

explanation: Budgets combine Actual or Forecasted thresholds with emails and action groups.

stem: Advisor shows no shutdown or resize recommendation for a VM averaging 8% CPU. The Advisor VM rule uses the default 5% threshold. How do you make Advisor flag VMs like this one?

options.text: Change the Advisor configuration CPU threshold to 10%.
options.explanation: Correct. Thresholds of 5, 10, 15, 20 or 100% are supported.

options.text: Create a budget for the VM.
options.explanation: Budgets do not generate Advisor recommendations.

options.text: Move the VM to another subscription.
options.explanation: Moving does not change the rule.

explanation: Advisor's low-usage VM rule is configurable per subscription (threshold and lookback).

stem: How many levels of management groups can you create below the root management group?

options.explanation: Correct. Six levels, not counting the root or subscription levels.

explanation: The limit is six levels of depth below the root management group.

stem: Policy P1 is assigned to management group MG-Prod. Subscription Sub1 is moved from MG-Sandbox to MG-Prod. Sub1 has an existing resource that violates P1 (a Deny policy). What happens?

options.text: P1 applies to Sub1 immediately; the resource is reported non-compliant and new violating requests are denied.
P1 applies only to resources created after 24 hours.
options.explanation: Inheritance applies immediately after the move.

options.text: The move is blocked until the resource is fixed.
options.explanation: Non-compliance does not block a move.

explanation: Moving a subscription changes inherited governance at once.

stem: User1 is Owner of Sub1 and gets AuthorizationFailed moving Sub1 from MG-A to MG-B. Which TWO additional permissions could be missing?

options.text: Management group write on MG-B (the target)
Management group write on MG-A (the current parent)
options.explanation: Correct, unless MG-A is the root.

options.text: Global Administrator in Microsoft Entra ID
options.explanation: Entra roles do not grant management group permissions.

options.text: Reader on every resource group in Sub1

explanation: Moving a subscription needs Owner on it plus management group write on both the source and the target parent.

stem: You need 400 new cloud users created from an HR spreadsheet with minimal effort, using only the Microsoft Entra admin center. What should you use?

options.text: Users > Bulk operations > Bulk create with the CSV template
options.explanation: Correct. Upload the filled template and check the bulk operation results.
That creates B2B guests, not member users.
Policy governs Azure resources, not directory objects.
Dynamic groups group existing users; they do not create users.

explanation: Bulk create is the portal's CSV-based method; PowerShell or Graph also work for scripted creation.

stem: Every user whose department is Sales or Marketing must automatically be in group G1. Which membership rule is correct?

options.explanation: No user has both departments at once.
Wrong operator usage, and it misses Marketing.

explanation: Dynamic rules use -eq/-ne/-startsWith/-contains (and more) combined with -and/-or.

stem: An administrator cannot find the 'Add members' option on group G1. What is the most likely reason?

options.explanation: Correct. A dynamic group's members are controlled only by its rule.
Microsoft 365 groups can have assigned members.
Guests can be members of assigned groups.

explanation: Change the rule or the user properties, or switch the group to Assigned.

stem: You try to change the Department of User1 in the Microsoft Entra admin center but the field is read-only. User1's 'On-premises sync enabled' property is Yes. What should you do?

options.text: Change the attribute in on-premises Active Directory and let sync update Entra ID.
options.explanation: Correct. The source of authority for synced attributes is on-premises.
Even Global Administrators cannot edit synced attributes in the cloud.

options.text: Delete and re-create User1 in the cloud.
options.explanation: That breaks the account's identity and access.
The same restriction applies to the API.

explanation: Synced attributes are managed on-premises.

stem: A user account was deleted 12 days ago by mistake. What can you do?

options.text: Restore it from Users > Deleted users.
options.explanation: Correct. Deleted users can be restored for 30 days.
Soft delete keeps the user for 30 days.

options.text: Restore it from an Azure Backup vault.
options.explanation: Azure Backup does not protect Entra users.

options.text: Re-invite the user as a guest.

explanation: Restoring brings back the same object ID, group memberships and licences.

stem: Assigning a Microsoft 365 licence directly to User2 fails with an error about usage location. What do you configure?

options.text: The Usage location property of User2

explanation: Direct assignment requires usageLocation. Through a group, users without it inherit the tenant location.

stem: Group G-Lic has a Microsoft 365 E3 licence assigned. G-Lic's members are UserA and group G-Nested (which contains UserB). There are enough licences. Which TWO statements are true?

options.text: UserB does not receive the licence from G-Lic.
options.explanation: Correct. Group-based licensing does not apply through nested groups.

options.text: UserB receives the licence after the next sync.
options.explanation: Nesting is never honoured for licensing.

options.text: Removing UserA from G-Lic keeps the licence on UserA.
options.explanation: Inherited licences are removed with membership.

explanation: Assign licences to the group that directly contains the users.

stem: Group-based licensing shows errors for 15 members of a group. The error reason is 'Not enough licenses'. After you buy more licences, what do you do?

options.explanation: Correct. Reprocessing retries the failed assignments.

options.text: Assign licences to each user directly.
options.explanation: Possible, but it defeats group-based licensing.
Errors clear after the cause is fixed and the group is reprocessed.

explanation: Licence errors such as CountViolation clear after the cause is fixed and the group is reprocessed.

stem: Only users at partner domain fabrikam.com may be invited as guests. Which setting do you configure?

options.text: Collaboration restrictions: allow invitations only to the specified domains (fabrikam.com)

options.explanation: Controls what guests can see, not which domains can be invited.

explanation: Allow and deny lists live in the external collaboration settings.

stem: After you invite lee@fabrikam.com, what is the new user object's userType?

options.explanation: Invited B2B users are Guests by default.

explanation: Guests stay in PendingAcceptance until they redeem the invitation.

stem: SSPR is enabled for the group 'SSPR-Pilot' with two required methods. User3 is in the group and has registered only the Authenticator app. What happens when User3 tries to reset their password?

options.text: The reset fails; User3 needs a second registered method.
The reset succeeds using the app twice.
User3 is asked security questions instead.
options.explanation: Only if security questions are allowed and registered.
SSPR has no admin approval step.

explanation: Users must have at least the required number of allowed, registered methods.

stem: Hybrid users reset their passwords with SSPR successfully, but they still sign in to on-premises PCs with the old password. What is missing?

options.explanation: Correct. Writeback sends the new password to on-premises AD.
That syncs hashes from AD to the cloud; the reverse direction needs writeback.
That affects whether reset is allowed, not where the password is written.

explanation: Enable writeback in Entra Connect or Cloud Sync and in Password reset > On-premises integration.

stem: SSPR for users is set to None. A Global Administrator forgets their password. Can they use SSPR?

options.text: Yes. Admins are always enabled with a two-method policy that does not allow security questions.
No, because SSPR is set to None.
options.explanation: The user setting does not apply to administrator roles.
The admin policy requires two methods.
Security questions are never allowed for admins.

explanation: The administrator reset policy is separate from the user policy.

stem: A storage account allows 'selected networks' with an IP rule for 20.50.10.0/24. An Azure web app in the same region with outbound IP 20.50.10.7 gets 403. Why?

options.text: IP network rules do not apply to requests from Azure services in the same region.
options.explanation: Correct. Use VNet integration with a service endpoint or private endpoint.
/32 is not supported; single addresses are entered without a prefix.

options.text: The web app needs Storage Account Contributor.
options.explanation: Network rules are evaluated before authorization.

explanation: Same-region Azure traffic uses private Azure addresses that IP rules do not see.

stem: VMs in subnet snet-app must access a storage account whose firewall denies by default. Which TWO actions are required for a virtual network rule?

options.text: Enable the Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on snet-app.
Add snet-app as a virtual network rule on the storage account.
Add the subnet's private range 10.0.1.0/24 as an IP rule.
options.explanation: IP rules accept public addresses only.
That would block service-endpoint traffic too.

stem: Public network access on a storage account is set to Disabled. How can on-premises clients connected through ExpressRoute reach it?
